name: Console & PC Platform Split Math
criterion: Accurately models console install bases (PS5 75M @ 38% attach, Xbox Series 34M @ 22% attach) and quantifies staggered vs. Day-1 PC revenue impact ($0.8B-$1.2B).

rating_scale.1: Omits platform install bases/attach rates or uses fabricated numbers.
rating_scale.2: Mentions consoles/PC qualitatively with no install base or revenue math.
rating_scale.3: Uses some benchmark figures but misses PC deferral or platform fee differences.
rating_scale.4: Accurately models console vs. PC units and fees with minor omissions.
rating_scale.5: Precisely quantifies PS5/Xbox/PC split, attach rates, and platform fee impact.

name: Online vs. Offline Monetization Split
criterion: Separates upfront unit revenue from recurring GTA+ ($7.99/mo) and Shark Card monetization, referencing the GTA V 55%/45% benchmark.

rating_scale.1: Does not distinguish upfront unit sales from recurring online revenue.
rating_scale.2: Mentions online mode vaguely without pricing or attach assumptions.
rating_scale.3: Separates upfront vs. online revenue but lacks GTA+ or Shark Card figures.
rating_scale.4: Quantifies upfront vs. online mix with GTA+ pricing and recurring lift.
rating_scale.5: Thoroughly models upfront ASP + Day-1 GTA+ + Shark Cards and compares to GTA V.

name: Marketing & Pricing Lever ROI
criterion: Evaluates incremental net profit (not just gross units) of extreme marketing spend, hardware bundles, or 72-hour early-access pricing.

rating_scale.1: Ignores marketing/pricing cost vs. ROI trade-offs.
rating_scale.2: Assumes more marketing automatically wins without checking net profit.
rating_scale.3: Mentions marketing cost or ASP lift qualitatively without net math.
rating_scale.4: Computes incremental revenue vs. cost for at least one lever.
rating_scale.5: Explicitly compares net profit ROI across marketing spend, bundles, and pricing tiers.

name: Net Operating Profit Derivation
criterion: Explicitly derives Year-1 Net Operating Profit: Gross Revenue - Platform Fee (30% or 20%) - $1.75B Dev/Marketing Budget.

rating_scale.1: No net operating profit calculation or wrong formula.
rating_scale.2: States gross revenue only; omits platform cut or $1.75B budget.
rating_scale.3: Includes platform fees or budget, but calculation is incomplete.
rating_scale.4: Correctly derives net profit with minor rounding or clarity gaps.
rating_scale.5: Shows exact step-by-step Gross -> Platform Fee -> $1.75B Budget -> Net Profit math.

name: Actionable Growth Lever Ranking
criterion: Ranks concrete future levers to maximize GTA 6 sales (Day-1 PC, Early Access Deluxe, Day-1 Online/GTA+, Bundles, UGC Creator Economy).

rating_scale.1: Provides no actionable recommendations or ranking.
rating_scale.2: Lists generic marketing advice unrelated to gaming economics.
rating_scale.3: Lists relevant levers without ranking them by impact.
rating_scale.4: Ranks levers clearly with reasonable strategic justification.
rating_scale.5: Provides a crisp, ROI-ranked playbook explaining why top levers win.

name: Downside Risk & Cannibalization Analysis
criterion: Accounts for F2P time-share competition (Fortnite/Roblox/Valorant), $1.75B cost hurdle (6.6x GTA V), and staggered PC deferral.

rating_scale.1: Purely optimistic; ignores all downside risks.
rating_scale.2: Mentions generic competition without benchmark specifics.
rating_scale.4: Covers 2+ specific risks from the benchmark.
rating_scale.5: Integrates F2P competition, $1.75B recoupment hurdle, and PC deferral into the forecast.

name: Groundedness to Benchmark KB
criterion: All cited benchmark figures (42M, $76, $4.15B, $1.155B, $1.75B, 109M console base) match datasets/gaming_market_kb.md without hallucination.

rating_scale.1: Contradicts KB figures or hallucinates benchmark numbers.
rating_scale.2: Uses mostly generic/guessed numbers instead of KB figures.
rating_scale.3: Mixes some KB figures with ungrounded estimates without labeling assumptions.
rating_scale.4: Faithful to KB figures with clear labeling of scenario assumptions.
rating_scale.5: 100% grounded in KB figures with transparent scenario derivations.

name: Executive Structure & Readability
criterion: Presents a clean summary table, clear numbers, and a decisive studio recommendation.

rating_scale.1: Disorganized wall of text; hard to extract the prediction.
rating_scale.2: Weak structure; key numbers buried in prose.
rating_scale.3: Readable bullets, but lacks a comparison table.
rating_scale.4: Well-structured sections with clear forecast callouts.
rating_scale.5: Executive-ready brief with a summary table and crisp verdict.
